newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan researchers find Roman ruins in north.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan researchers find Roman ruins in north.

text.p: Moroccan archaeologists have uncovered a large Roman military camp in northern Morocco in a region where such finds had not previously been made, the Cultural Affairs Ministry said on Tuesday.
The camp was discovered near the Moroccan coastal town of Larache.

The find "opens news horizons for archaeological and historical research on the Roman period and particularly that concerning relations between the Roman authorities and native tribes," the ministry said.
In a statement it said the camp was obviously a major base, and had two gates on the north and south sides, each six metres (19.5 ft) wide.
Nearby were remains of doors and blocks from the internal buildings, the ministry said, quoted by the official news agency MAP.
"A watchtower...on Tarkount hill, at an altitude of 176 metres (572 ft) enabled it to control a vast zone and give the signal to the soldiers in the camp in case of danger," it said.
The same team of archaeologists had also found traces of Phoenician occupation near the town of Ksar El Kebir, which lies some 30 km (20 miles) inland from Larache, the ministry said.
